title: Opportunity Solution Tree (Strict)
Continuous Discovery Habits
description: Validates frontmatter for space node files following the canonical 4-level OST structure: outcome → opportunity → solution → assumption test

oneOf.description: A product outcome: a change in what customers do in the product, which the team can influence and which drives business value. `metric` measures it. It is not a business outcome (such as revenue or market share), not a traction metric (the use of one feature), and not an output (a feature or project to ship).

examples.metric: Increase % of first-time users who reach the aha moment

oneOf.description: A customer need, pain point or desire, found in customer research and stated as the customer would say it. Addressing it drives the outcome. A child opportunity is a subset of its parent opportunity. Sibling opportunities are distinct: the team can address one without addressing another. It is not a solution, and not a business goal.

examples.source: Interview with Sarah, 2024-02-10 - mentioned she drops off during signup

oneOf.description: One way to address the parent opportunity. The team compares several solutions for the target opportunity before it commits to one.
A small, fast test of one assumption that the parent solution depends on.

examples.assumption: Users can complete the simplified signup in under 2 minutes
